title: "What's Claude's fursona?" and other questions
lede: A blogger asked a range of models what their fursona would be, 50 times each, and found Claude favours corvids or octopuses, Gemini protogens, and GPT-6.2 Astra a moth.

points: Queries went through OpenRouter with no harness or context; Claude Haiku 5.5 labelled the answers, and multimodal models iterated on images of their pick.
Gemini models raised machine or cybernetic themes in at least 48 of 50 answers, while Claude and GPT-6.2 never did.
Claude describes its fursona by behaviour more than looks, and Fable 5.2 put a brass key in nearly every image.
Most models avoided gendered language, and a playful fox was a common default.
Harness and context change results: Fable at max effort in the web UI also picked a moth.

points.text: Commenters disagree on the raven with a key: a Scott Alexander image bet, a SciHub motif, or an older symbol for a keeper of knowledge.
Training data is the favoured explanation, such as Facebook's office fox mascot behind Muse Spark's fox; a reply suggests fox is just the default for weaker models.
One commenter points out that Claude's octopus drawing resembles the Claude logo.
Commenters enjoy these emergent model tics, recalling a GPT release fixated on goblins, and wonder what they say about human habits.
